content.text: In Nigeria, where traditional payment platforms are restricted, entrepreneurs like you face a daunting challenge: how to sell digital products without being locked out by Stripe, Gumroad, or PayPal. This guide shows you how to build a crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, leveraging COREMERCH's infrastructure and NOWPayments to accept crypto payments for free, without relying on these platforms. By the end of this post, you'll have a fully-functional digital store up and running, processing transactions and delivering products to your customers. Let's get started.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

COREMERCH's infrastructure is designed to bypass traditional payment platforms, giving you complete control over your digital commerce stack. With GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, and Supabase, you can host, deploy, and manage your store without relying on Stripe, PayPal, or Gumroad. NOWPayments, a low-fee crypto payment processor, integrates seamlessly with your stack, ensuring secure and fast transactions. By decentralizing your payment and delivery pipeline, you're not vulnerable to platform restrictions or shutdowns.
What You Need Before You Deploy

To deploy a crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, you'll need a GitHub account, a Cloudflare account, and a NOWPayments account. You'll also need to create a Supabase instance for order storage and a Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 account for file delivery. Don't worry, these services are free or low-cost, and COREMERCH provides comprehensive documentation and support to help you get started.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

With your accounts set up, it's time to configure your payment and delivery pipeline. You'll need to connect your NOWPayments account to your Cloudflare Pages store, set up a Supabase instance for order storage, and configure a Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 account for file delivery. This process may seem complex, but COREMERCH's documentation and support team are here to guide you every step of the way.
With COREMERCH's infrastructure, you can accept crypto payments without relying on traditional payment platforms.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Testing before promotion is not optional — it is the step that determines whether your store functions correctly under real conditions before real buyers encounter it. The test sequence has four steps. First: deploy the backend — Cloudflare Worker or Apps Script Web App — and confirm the webhook endpoint returns a valid response to a test HTTP POST. Second: configure the storefront and confirm the checkout displays correctly on desktop and mobile, QR codes generate, and live price feeds load. Third: complete a real mainnet transaction with a small amount of actual crypto — send real USDT or BTC to your configured wallet address and confirm in your NOWPayments dashboard that the transaction was detected and the webhook was fired. Fourth: check your order database — Supabase or Google Sheets — and confirm the order was logged correctly, the delivery email arrived, and the download link works. Only after all four steps confirm should you share the store URL publicly.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your digital store grows, you'll need to scale your infrastructure to keep up with demand. COREMERCH's Complete Builder Kit provides everything you need to build, deploy, and scale a sovereign digital commerce stack. With this kit, you'll have access to all 6 blueprints, 7 templates, and comprehensive documentation to help you optimize your infrastructure for high-traffic and high-revenue stores.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The setup sequence matters because each component depends on the previous one being correctly configured. Start with NOWPayments: create your account, configure wallet addresses for each coin you want to accept, generate the API key, and note the IPN secret key you will set. Then configure the backend: in Stack 01, deploy the Google Apps Script Web App and note its URL; in Stack 02, deploy the Cloudflare Worker and note its URL. Set that URL as the webhook endpoint in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Then configure the storefront: Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages with your product pages and checkout flow pointing to the backend. Then run a real mainnet test — send actual crypto to your configured wallet address, confirm NOWPayments detects it, confirm the webhook fires to your backend, confirm the order appears in your database, and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link. Only after the complete pipeline test passes should you make the store URL public. COREMERCH runs this complete test before handoff on every deployment.
